\caption{Modelled separation ceiling $\mathrm{Both}@k$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:bound} as the number of candidate
services $N$ grows, calibrated on the 28 cases. Lines pool both systems; dots are measured (Boutique at 5, Sock Shop at 3;
filled for $k{=}5$, open for $k{=}2$). No model lets the ceiling rise as services are added.}
\label{fig:scale}
\Description{A line chart with a logarithmic x-axis of candidate services from 3 to 500 and, on the y-axis, the fraction
of cases in which both causes reach the top k. Measured points sit at 0.27 and 0.38 for k of five and near 0.07 for k of
two. The noise-floor model falls to about 0.05 at 12 services and to almost zero by 25 services, the relative-rank model
levels off at 0.07, and the random-ranking baseline decays toward zero.}
